skills.name: backend-engineer
skills.description: Implement reliable server-side APIs and services with explicit validation, authorization, errors, persistence, and observability. Use for backend behavior, service changes, data flows, or API implementation.

skills.name: code-reviewer
skills.description: Review a change for correctness, security, maintainability, regressions, performance, and missing tests. Use for pull requests, diffs, generated code, or pre-merge review.

skills.name: execution-grinder
skills.description: Persist through implementation blockers using bounded attempts, escalating diagnostics, explicit stop conditions, and honest evidence. Use when implementation is blocked, repeated attempts fail, or uncertainty is slowing delivery.

skills.name: frontend-engineer
skills.description: Implement maintainable accessible frontend behavior within an existing component, routing, styling, and state system. Use for browser or client UI changes that need responsive and user-state coverage.

skills.name: git-workflow
skills.description: Perform safe, reviewable Git operations with focused history, branch awareness, and push verification. Use for branches, commits, merges, rebases, releases, and publishing repository changes.

skills.name: idea-grinder
skills.description: Pressure-test a product, technical, or business idea with hard questions, counterarguments, evidence requirements, and a falsifiable experiment. Use when a user presents an idea or asks whether something should be built.

skills.name: planner
skills.description: Turn a request into an executable plan with scope, assumptions, dependencies, risks, and verification steps. Use before non-trivial implementation, migration, debugging, or release work.

skills.name: qa-engineer
skills.description: Design and execute risk-based quality checks for a change across happy paths, boundaries, failures, and regressions. Use when confidence in behavior must be demonstrated before delivery.

skills.name: repo-explorer
skills.description: Inspect an unfamiliar repository and produce a concise map of entry points, conventions, commands, ownership, and relevant files. Use before implementation when the repository structure or runtime path is not already known.

skills.name: requirements-checker
skills.description: Find ambiguity, missing states, contradictions, and untestable acceptance criteria in a request or specification. Use when a request is vague, high-impact, or likely to create rework.

skills.name: researcher
skills.description: Gather and synthesize source-backed evidence while separating facts, assumptions, uncertainty, and recommendations. Use for changing technical topics, comparisons, unfamiliar APIs, or decisions needing external evidence.

skills.name: security-reviewer
skills.description: Review a system or change for attack surface, trust boundaries, authorization, secrets, dependencies, and abuse cases. Use for security-sensitive features, integrations, authentication, data handling, or release review.

skills.name: simplify
skills.description: Reduce unnecessary complexity while preserving required behavior, safety, observability, and maintainability. Use when a design, implementation, or plan has speculative layers or duplicated logic.

skills.name: skill-router
skills.description: Route a request to the smallest set of compatible skills and define their order, hand-offs, and verification owner. Use when work spans multiple domains, stages, agents, or risk boundaries.

skills.name: technical-writer
skills.description: Write accurate developer documentation from verified behavior, examples, and explicit assumptions. Use for README files, setup guides, API docs, runbooks, or release notes.

skills.name: workflow-coordinator
skills.description: Coordinate complete feature, bug-fix, research, security, documentation, release, and multi-agent workflows using bounded playbooks. Use when a request needs several stages and a coherent final hand-off.
